newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles Int'l airport unveils expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles Int'l airport unveils expansion plans.

text.p: The Los Angeles Department of Airports on Friday unveiled multi-billion dollar plans to modernize the Los Angeles International Airport to accommodate growing passenger and cargo demands for the next 20 years.

The proposed airport improvements could run from $8 billion to $12 billion, depending on the projects undertaken. These cost estimates could change by 30 percent either way, airport spokeswoman Susan Gilmore said.
The projects would be funded primarily with revenue bonds, Gilmore said.

Airport Commission President Dan Garcia said the airport master plan, unveiled in Los Angeles on Friday, represented "our region's best opportunity to secure jobs and an economic future for the next generation of Los Angeles residents."

The four development scenarios under consideration include a new terminal building and four new concourses, an automated people mover system and roadway, new cargo facilities and a limited access circulation road around the airport.

The first proposal calls for five runways, while the second and third each have six runways. The fourth proposal would include the use of nearby Hawthorne Airport as a commuter runway with connections to Los Angeles International.

"The proposed expansion will accommodate the dramatic growth in international markets, meet travelers' demands for easy access to destinations around the world and create economic opportunities for Angelenos well into the 21st Century," Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan said.
According to an airport study, in the base year of 1994, $43.5 billion in economic activity, and 393,000 jobs, were directly related to the Los Angeles International Airport.

The same study found that by 2015, the impact of the airport on the local economy will grow to $64.3 billion and 472,000 jobs, but only if it is modernized to allow it to handle up to 98 million passengers.
If Los Angeles International does not modernize, up to 367,000 jobs in the Los Angeles region could be lost when indirect economic effects are included, the study said.

In 1994, the airport served 51 million passengers and shipped 1.7 million tons of cargo to destinations worldwide. Forecasts indicate that by 2015, 98 million passengers will use the airport annually, and the annual cargo use will reach 4.2 million tons.
The airport master plan is a long-range blueprint for development over the next 20 years.
